title: Why Shouldn’t Amazon Spinoff AWS And Annapurna Labs?
gist: Timothy Prickett Morgan uses the EMC/VMware precedent to argue Amazon could unlock value by floating 20-30 percent minority stakes in Annapurna Labs, AWS, and its media/advertising arm while retaining majority control. The supporting numbers: Annapurna custom silicon at a >$25 billion annualized run rate growing triple digits (which Jassy says would be ~$50-60 billion if sold as merchant chips rather than rented as EC2), AWS Q2 revenue of $42.23 billion up 36.8 percent with a $496 billion backlog, and 2026 capex guidance raised 10 percent to $220 billion - though Morgan warns a chunk of AWS's revenue acceleration is component-vendor price gouging, not new demand.

insights.claim: EMC bought VMware for $635 million in cash in December 2003 just before its planned IPO, a company that had raised only $25 million across two rounds, and took it public in summer 2007 at a $26 billion market capitalization.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A ~40x value creation inside a parent in under four years is the template being invoked for Annapurna Labs - the argument that hidden subsidiary value can be crystallized by a public float.
insights.quote: EMC swooped in with $635 million in cash – an offer that co-founders and spouses Diane Greene and Mendel Rosenblum could not refuse.
insights.locator: One of the most diabolically clever things that EMC

insights.claim: VMware has generated on the order of $160 billion in cumulative revenue across its history and is now a profitable, slowly growing part of Broadcom after passing through EMC, Dell, a 2021 spinout, and Hock Tan's take-private.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The asset survived four ownership structures and kept compounding - evidence that repeated financial engineering around a genuinely good business does not destroy it, which lowers the perceived risk of an Amazon carve-out.
insights.quote: VMware has probably brought in on the order of $160 billion in revenues in its history thus far, and is a profitable and slowly growing part of the Broadcom empire.
insights.locator: In 2021, Dell spun out the huge chunk of VMware

insights.claim: The rational objection to subsidiary spinouts is that shareholders already own the subsidiary through the parent's stock, yet markets have repeatedly rewarded these structures anyway.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Conglomerate-discount arbitrage works on sentiment, not arithmetic - so bet on the structure being rewarded even when it adds no economic value.
insights.quote: I have always contended that there was no way for EMC or Dell to sell VMware to Wall Street because investors already owned VMware by virtue of holding stock in EMC and then Dell.
insights.locator: I have always contended

insights.claim: Markets in the current attention economy do not need to make economic sense, only to provoke reaction that someone can profit from - the author's explicit reason for abandoning his own literal objection to spinouts.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A cynical but tradeable framing: corporate-structure announcements move stocks on narrative, so position for the announcement rather than the fundamentals.
insights.quote: the world, meaning our collective action driven by very human forces, does not have to make sense. It does not have to make sense.
insights.locator: With more years under my belt

insights.claim: The specific structure proposed is not a full separation but minority floats of roughly 20 to 30 percent in Annapurna Labs, AWS, and the media/advertising businesses, with Amazon retaining majority stakes in each.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A minority float would force segment-level disclosure and give the market a pure-play comparable for custom AI silicon - the disclosure itself is the value unlock, not the cash raised.
insights.quote: Don’t think I have lost my mind here – I am not talking about complete spinouts. But maybe 20 percent or 30 percent stakes, with the Amazon mothership holding majority stakes.
insights.locator: Don’t think I have lost my mind here

insights.claim: A standalone Annapurna Labs would be forced to disclose its payments to AWS for chip development and its chip sales revenue from AWS, Anthropic, and OpenAI - transfer pricing that is currently invisible inside Amazon.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The true economics of hyperscaler custom silicon - whether it is genuinely cheaper than buying NVIDIA - are unknowable until such a carve-out forces disclosure.
insights.quote: If Annapurna was spun out, it would have to show its payments to AWS for chip development as well as how much money it gets by selling chips to AWS and soon Anthropic and OpenAI
insights.locator: It is hard to know if the value of Annapurna Labs is baked in

insights.claim: Whether the market has priced Annapurna Labs into Amazon stock at all is genuinely unclear, but the custom silicon business demonstrably improves Amazon's margins.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: If custom silicon is not in the price, Amazon holds an unrecognized asset comparable to a top-three merchant chip vendor - the core of the bull case for the stock at a $3 trillion cap.
insights.quote: It is hard to know if the value of Annapurna Labs is baked into the Amazon stock price or not.
insights.locator: It is hard to know if the value of Annapurna Labs

insights.claim: Amazon's structure is described as businesses nested inside businesses at a market capitalization above $3 trillion, which is the underlying conglomerate-discount setup for the thought experiment.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Watch for activist pressure on Amazon's structure; the nested-conglomerate framing is exactly the argument activists deploy before demanding separations.
insights.quote: which has businesses nested inside of businesses and which has attained a market capitalization in excess of $3 trillion
insights.locator: And so, as I contemplate the financials

insights.claim: Amazon's chip unit - Graviton CPUs, Trainium XPUs, and Nitro DPUs - grew 40 percent versus Q4 2025 and exited Q1 2026 at an annualized run rate above $20 billion.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: 40 percent sequential growth in a $20 billion business is a direct share transfer away from merchant silicon vendors selling into AWS.
insights.quote: grew by 40 percent compared to Q4 2025 and had an annualized run rate of over $20 billion as the first quarter of 2026 ended
insights.locator: In that letter to shareholders

insights.claim: By Q2 2026 the Annapurna Labs custom silicon business reached an annualized run rate of more than $25 billion while still growing at triple-digit rates.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Triple-digit growth off a $25 billion base makes Amazon internal silicon one of the fastest-growing semiconductor franchises anywhere - a structural headwind for merchant CPU and accelerator share.
insights.quote: the Annapurna Labs custom silicon business has an annualized run rate of more than $25 billion and is still experiencing triple digit growth
insights.locator: This time around in Q2 2026

insights.claim: Andy Jassy claims Amazon's custom silicon business is now one of the top three datacenter chip businesses in the world, and emphasizes the speed at which it got there.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: If accepted, this places Amazon alongside NVIDIA and one other vendor in datacenter silicon without Amazon ever selling a chip on the merchant market - a category the sell-side does not currently model.
insights.quote: As best as we can tell, our custom silicon business is now one of the top three datacenter chip businesses in the world
insights.locator: This time around in Q2 2026

insights.claim: Jassy said the homegrown chip business would run at roughly a $50 billion annualized rate if sold externally rather than rented as EC2 capacity, and the author extrapolates the Q2 figure to imply about $60 billion in theoretical external revenue.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The ~2.4x gap between rental run rate and merchant-equivalent revenue quantifies how much value AWS captures by keeping silicon captive - and what a spun-out Annapurna could theoretically address.
insights.quote: Jassy also said that if AWS sold its homegrown chips to the outside world rather than renting them as EC2 capacity, it would have an annualized run rate of around $50 billion.
insights.locator: In that letter to shareholders

insights.claim: Graviton CPUs were in use by more than 130,000 customers at the end of Q2 2026, up 45 percent year on year.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Arm-based general-purpose compute adoption is broadening fast, not concentrating in a few whales - a durable erosion of the x86 server CPU total addressable market.
insights.quote: The Graviton CPU is now being used by more than 130,000 customers as of the end of Q2 2026, an increase of 45 percent year on year.
insights.locator: This implies that the theoretical external revenue

insights.claim: Trainium 2 and Trainium 3 capacity is largely booked out for the next two years, which Jassy cited in his April shareholder letter as the basis for AWS's confidence in its AI capex.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Pre-booked multi-year accelerator capacity converts AI capex from a speculative bet into contracted backlog - the strongest single argument against the AI-overbuild thesis at AWS.
insights.quote: The company’s Trainium 2 and Trainium 3 capacity for the next two years is largely booked out
insights.locator: AWS is riding the GenAI boom high

insights.claim: Two separate hyperscalers offered to buy out the entire year's worth of AWS Graviton capacity for all of 2026, indicating general-purpose CPU supply is as constrained as AI accelerator supply.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Rival hyperscalers bidding for a competitor's internal CPU output is an extreme scarcity signal - general-purpose compute shortage is an underappreciated second front alongside GPUs.
insights.quote: Not one, but two hyperscalers offered to buy out the entire year’s worth of all Graviton capacity for all of 2026. That’s how crazy it is out there.
insights.locator: And it is not just GPUs and Trainiums that are selling

insights.claim: Anthropic and OpenAI have together commissioned gigawatts of Trainium datacenter capacity for model building, making frontier labs direct customers of Amazon's silicon rather than only NVIDIA's.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Frontier-lab validation of a non-NVIDIA training stack at gigawatt scale is the most consequential competitive datapoint here - it breaks the assumption that serious training requires CUDA.
insights.quote: soon Anthropic and OpenAI, which have commissioned gigawatts of combined Trainium datacenter capacity to drive their model building
insights.locator: If Annapurna was spun out

insights.claim: The AWS revenue backlog stands at $496 billion.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Backlog of roughly three times trailing annualized AWS revenue underwrites the capex program and gives multi-year revenue visibility that the market may still be discounting.
insights.quote: The AWS revenue backlog stands at a staggering $496 billion.
insights.locator: The AWS revenue backlog

insights.claim: Amazon's Q2 2026 revenue was $200.61 billion, up 19.6 percent, with operating income up 43.2 percent to $27.46 billion.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Operating leverage of roughly 2:1 over revenue growth at $200 billion scale is the number that supports the $3 trillion valuation.
insights.quote: the combined groups and divisions of Amazon had revenues of $200.61 billion, up 19.6 percent. Operating income rose by 43.2 percent to $27.46 billion
insights.locator: In the second quarter

insights.claim: Amazon's reported net income of $62.65 billion, up 2.45x year on year, was driven by a $53.4 billion non-operating gain on its OpenAI investment rather than by the operating businesses.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Roughly 85 percent of headline net income is a mark-to-market gain on a private AI stake - a reminder that hyperscaler earnings now carry embedded AI-valuation beta that reverses if private marks fall.
insights.quote: thanks to a $53.4 billion gain on its investment in OpenAI, parent Amazon posted net income of $62.65 billion, up 2.45X year on year
insights.locator: In the second quarter

insights.claim: AWS posted $42.23 billion of Q2 revenue, up 36.8 percent year on year and 12.4 percent sequentially, with operating income of $16.62 billion up 63.6 percent year on year but only 17.4 percent sequentially.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The gap between the year-on-year and sequential operating income growth rates is where margin expansion is decelerating - the sequential series is the honest read on AI-era AWS profitability.
insights.quote: AWS operating income came to $16.62 billion, up and even more impressive 63.6 percent year on year but up only 17.4 percent sequentially.
insights.locator: In the quarter, the AWS business

insights.claim: AWS is growing faster than at any point in four and a half years, with the GenAI boom reviving growth for AWS overall and for compute in particular.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Cloud re-acceleration is real and AI-driven; the pre-2025 narrative of a maturing, decelerating AWS is obsolete.
insights.quote: it is the fastest growth that AWS has seen in four and a half years
insights.locator: The interesting bit about this GenAI boom

insights.claim: Amazon raised its 2026 capex guidance by 10 percent to $220 billion, and the increase is attributed mainly to system component price increases rather than to expanded buildout plans.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A capex raise driven by input inflation rather than volume means less compute per dollar - bearish for the efficiency of the AI buildout even as it is bullish for component suppliers.
insights.quote: The company raised its capex guidance by 10 percent for 2026, to $220 billion, mainly driven by system component price increases.
insights.locator: Most of that cash was blown on capital expenses

insights.claim: Datacenter shells and IT equipment run on completely different capital cycles: datacenter capital is spent two years before servers can be installed but then monetizes for 30-plus years, while servers are bought only months ahead of deployment.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Splitting hyperscaler capex into a 30-year real-estate component and a 3-6 year IT component is the correct way to assess overbuild risk - only the second half can be stranded.
insights.quote: Once a datacenter opens with servers plugged in, we start generating significant revenue right away and then get to monetize these data centers for 30-plus years without having to spend that start-up capital again.
insights.locator: Jassy explained the capex situation to Wall Street

insights.claim: AWS claims it has strong demand visibility before committing server spend and will simply not spend the capital if demand is absent, positioning server capex as demand-following rather than speculative.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The explicit rebuttal to the AI-overbuild bear case; the falsifiable test is whether AWS actually cuts server orders in a demand air pocket.
insights.quote: we have strong visibility into customer demand before we trigger the spend. If the demand isn't there, we won't spend the capital.
insights.locator: Servers and networking equipment operate on a shorter cycle

insights.claim: Servers break even in a little under three years, have a useful life of at least five to six years, and most AI capacity is contracted for at least five-year terms - meaning two to three years of significant free cash flow per server after breakeven.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Contract duration matching useful life is what makes AI infrastructure cash-generative rather than a treadmill; watch for any shortening of either number as the leading indicator of deterioration.
insights.quote: The servers currently have a useful life of at least five to six years, and most of our AI capacity these days is being contracted for at least five-year terms.
insights.locator: For servers and networking equipment

insights.claim: Part of the AWS operating income increase comes from keeping hardware in the field longer and depreciating it more slowly rather than from underlying operational gains, and the author believes Jassy is understating how much money this produces.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Depreciation-life extension is an accounting lever that inflates reported margins; it is finite and reverses, so strip it out when modelling sustainable AWS operating margin.
insights.quote: I think Jassy is being modest. AWS generates a hell of a lot of money from keeping that stuff in the field.
insights.locator: Some of this increase in operating income

insights.claim: A portion of AWS's accelerating revenue growth is not new business but pass-through of opportunistic price increases by component makers who have clouds, hyperscalers, and OEMs over a barrel.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Cloud revenue growth is being flattered by input inflation, so unit-demand growth is weaker than headline percentages suggest - a reason to discount cloud top-line acceleration in 2026.
insights.quote: opportunistic shakedowns by the component makers who have clouds, hyperscalers, and OEMs over a barrel
insights.locator: But remember

insights.claim: Price increases across DRAM, flash, CPUs, and GPUs are expected to accelerate AWS revenue growth rates in coming quarters, meaning reported cloud growth will overstate real demand further.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Expect an inflation-driven beat in cloud revenue over the next few quarters that is not margin-accretive - buy the memory suppliers, fade the cloud multiple expansion.
insights.quote: And given the price increases on DRAM, flash, CPUs, and GPUs, the revenue growth rate will only accelerate in the coming quarters.
insights.locator: The interesting bit about this GenAI boom

insights.claim: Amazon has never disclosed any breakdown of AWS revenue across compute, storage, networking, and software, so even specialist estimates of that mix are acknowledged guesswork.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The disclosure vacuum is itself the argument for the spinout thesis - and a caution against any model that assumes a known AWS compute-versus-storage revenue split.
insights.quote: This is admittedly a total fabrication based on hunches along, since Amazon has never given any hints about such a breakdown.
insights.locator: Every quarter, I take my best stab
